lp_title: Decision Rooms · Decide together, on facts
lp_desc: Decision Rooms helps leaders and organisations make better decisions together: grounded in facts, honest about disagreement, accountable for how they turn out.
lp_h1: Decide together, on facts, with every voice heard.
lp_sub: Bring your question, your files and what's happening in the world into one room. Everyone answers privately, a proven decision model does the thinking, and you get one clear call with the reasoning shown.
lp_f1_c: people is where group decisions peak
lp_f1_f: Each person beyond seven cuts decision effectiveness by about 10%. Groups of 17 or more rarely decide at all.
lp_f2_c: of leaders say their organisation excels at decision making
lp_f2_f: Most say the process is slow, political or unclear about who decides.
lp_f3_c: of leaders' time goes into making decisions
lp_f3_f: And more than half of that time, they say, is used ineffectively.
lp_f4_c: more reasons for failure surface when a team imagines it already happened
lp_f4_f: That's the idea behind the pre-mortem, which every room runs before it makes a call.
lp_f4_s: Mitchell, Russo & Pennington (1989); Gary Klein, HBR (2007)
lp_s1_b: Write the question, the options and what everyone should know. Add files if you have them.
lp_s2_b: Share one link. Each person says, in about two minutes and in private, what matters to them and how much risk they can live with.
lp_s3_b: A proven decision model, recommended for your question, weighs the options against live facts and every member's view.
lp_s4_b: A recommendation with its reasons, the risks, where the group differs, and tripwires that tell you when to rethink.
lp_s5_b: The owner decides on the record, everyone signs off, and on the review date the room checks how it turned out.
lp_models_t: Proven ways of thinking, built in
lp_models_b: Every room uses a decision model from the world's best strategy teams. We recommend one for your question; you can choose another.
lp_get_b: One recommendation, the reasoning behind it, and an honest picture of where the group agrees and where it splits. Never who said what.
lp_mock_q: Should we open a second office in Dubai this year?
lp_mock_h: Wait a year and serve the Gulf remotely, while testing whether local presence is really blocking sales.
lp_mock_split: Cash risk: the group is split
lp_t1_b: Each person's answers are visible only to them, enforced in the database. The group sees the combined result, never who said what.
lp_t2_b: Your questions and files are used only to produce your decision. We never sell them or use them to train AI models. Storage is encrypted.
lp_t3_b: Public-affairs rooms decide only from the group's own stated values and show the strongest case for each side.
lp_t4_b: The recommendation supports your judgement. The owner decides, and any override is recorded with the reason.
lp_plans_b: Everything is free while we run the trial. These are the plans we'll offer after it.
lp_p1_l: Up to 8 members · 10 rooms a month · All decision models · Reviews
lp_p2_l: Several workspaces · More rooms and members · RAPID roles · Priority support
lp_p3_l: A room plus a session with a human facilitator, for succession, a partner exit or a public stance
lp_end_t: Your next big call deserves more than the loudest voice in the room.
lp_rights: Decision Rooms supports decisions; it doesn't replace professional advice.

paste_ph: Paste a Slack thread, an email or any conversation here
how_wa_ios: Tap the name at the top.
Scroll down and tap Export Chat.
Choose Without Media (or Attach Media; we only read the text).
Save it to Files or send it to yourself, then add the file here.
how_wa_and: Tap Export chat and choose Without media.
Save it or send it to yourself, then add the file here.
how_slack: For a thread: open it, select the messages and copy them.
Tap Paste a conversation here and paste it.
For a whole channel (workspace admins): Workspace settings → Import/Export Data → Export, then add the .zip here.
how_email: Pick Save as PDF, then add the PDF here.
how_docs: Word and PDF files can be added as they are.
In Google Docs: File → Download → Microsoft Word or PDF.
how_sheets: Excel and CSV files can be added as they are.
In Google Sheets: File → Download → Microsoft Excel or CSV.
how_tip: Scanned PDFs (photos of pages) have no text we can read, so use the original file when you can.
